verdict: NOT CERTIFIED; proceed only with relabeling. No candidate can be certified as unsolved, because search silence is not evidence. No candidate can be certified as 'not too hard'; every difficulty judgment here is inference. SOF decoupling fails the literal openness screen. Stochastic preview and visual cryptography are under-specified and at high risk of being swapped for restatements. Robust SPR (uniform in n) and P-type ILC are the most defensible 'no resolution located' candidates. No 'solved' label is supportable on current evidence.

findings.issue: 'Unsolved' rests on the book's 2011 status plus a search, and search silence cannot establish openness. The referee cannot verify the Sept-2026 preprints or the fetched Chen et al. text, so any judgment that uses them depends on the parent's reading.
findings.required_correction: Give each candidate exactly one label: 'no resolution located (search log, as of 2026-10-14)', 'publicly claimed resolved, unverified', 'resolved in principle', or 'ill-posed as stated'. Each search log must cover forward citations of the book entry and of the key pre-2011 papers, with page or theorem locators.

findings.issue: Read literally (find K, with or without Hurwitz A+BKC1), the problem is a set of polynomial equations in K: the Markov parameters for j=0..n−1 vanish and D22+D2KD1=0, plus Routh–Hurwitz inequalities for the stable variant. Tarski–Seidenberg makes this decidable, and Chen et al. 2000 (as fetched) gives an explicit Gröbner/QEPCAD procedure that predates the book. Setting E=0, D1=0, D22=0 recovers SOF stabilization. So the parent-reported NP-hardness, if correct, carries over to the with-stability variant but not automatically to pure decoupling. Hardness also only limits algorithms; it does not answer the question.
findings.required_correction: Quote the book's exact demand. If the text asks for no structural criterion, label the problem 'resolved in principle; book status stale' and replace it from the screened pages. If it does, write that criterion out verbatim before attacking, and do not add an efficiency requirement.

findings.issue: For each fixed n the claim is a Tarski sentence (for all bounds, there exists b, for all ω), so it is decidable in principle. Any per-degree result, including n=7, is a special case; the original is uniform in n>4. 'Not too hard' is doubtful (inference): the next two degrees were reportedly settled only in 2026 preprints, one degree at a time, with machine checking. Those claims have not been replayed. Nobody has confirmed that the Lean statement matches the book: exact-degree-n numerator, the ω→∞ limit, and one b for the whole family.
findings.required_correction: Cite n=5/6 as 'publicly claimed, not independently verified', and check the Lean statement before treating n≥7 as the frontier. Replaying the proof is not needed for the selection decision. Keep the target at all n>4. A counterexample counts only with exact data and a checkable certificate.

findings.issue: The book's criterion E‖z‖/E‖w‖<γ is not quadratic, and the filtration and x(0) conventions are unspecified. By Jensen, for deterministic w a mean-square bound E‖z‖²<γ²‖w‖² implies the literal bound, but only as a sufficient condition. For random w, Jensen gives no implication. A mean-square necessary-and-sufficient theorem therefore does not answer the book's question.
findings.required_correction: State both readings and every convention: whether w is deterministic or adapted, how w relates to W, and the information pattern. Label mean-square results 'standard reformulation'. The contributor's notation in their own papers is evidence of intent, not proof.

findings.issue: For any fixed access structure, all four optima are finite LP/ILP optima. Solver pipelines and n≤4 tables are therefore restatements. The form a general answer should take is undefined, and conventions for contrast and for strong vs weak structures vary. A characterization over all monotone structures is unlikely to be easy (inference).
findings.required_correction: Fix the model and the contrast definition from the book. Define what counts as a general answer: a formula or characterization, or constructions with matching lower bounds, valid for every monotone structure. Treat tables as evidence only, and check first whether such tables are already published.

findings.issue: With relative degree ≥1, e_k(0) depends only on the initial state. Under u_{k+1}=u_k+Le_k, a repeated initial error with Le(0)≠0 gives u_k(0)=u_0(0)+kLe(0), so inputs grow without bound and exact tracking on [0,T] is impossible. This elementary fact frames the question; it is not a result, and no Volterra example is needed to show it. The target, the nonlinear class, and the allowed modifications are unspecified. Existing initial-rectification designs may already meet a reasonable formalization.
findings.required_correction: Formalize the norm, the nonlinear class, the allowed modifications (from the book text), and the target. Target: an error bound uniform over iterations, proportional to the initial-error and disturbance bounds, with no residual bias when they vanish. Check rectification designs against exactly this before calling the problem open. Reset schemes for scalar plants are special cases.

findings.issue: Launching five agents is not the same as attacking five original problems. Without closure gates, outputs for fixed n, scalar plants, threshold structures, mean-square variants, and decision procedures will drift into the summary as progress.
findings.required_correction: Close each agent only when it supplies: the verbatim statement and page; a ledger of interpretive choices; a list of deviations; a result typed as full, partial (exact scope), negative-for-variant, or none; and an independent check of any proof. Label solver, QE, LP, SOS, and Riccati outputs as computation.

findings.issue: The 'first pages' provenance and the screening order are not recorded. The replacements for the two removed problems may come from outside that page range.
findings.required_correction: For every screened entry (selected, removed, excluded), list the page number and a one-line reason, and record the criteria in the order applied.

recommended_order.rationale: This is the crispest falsifiable statement: a uniform proof or one certified counterexample settles it. Immediate step: Re(b·ā)(iω)=b_E a_E+b_O a_O is linear in (a_E,a_O). For each ω, (a_E,a_O) ranges over a rectangle whose corners are the four Kharitonov values. So the condition is exactly a common SPR numerator for K1–K4. Because b must be Hurwitz, arg b(iω) increases and must stay inside a frequency-dependent corridor. Options: try a uniform Hermite–Biehler interlacing construction, or search n≥7 families near the stability boundary, where the corridor narrows. Likely hard (inference).

Once formalized, this is a concrete design question, and the t=0 obstruction is a sharp benchmark. First finish the comparison with the rectification literature. If a gap remains (nonlinear class, initial errors that vary between iterations), prove iteration-uniform bounds for a P-type law that does not accumulate the input-independent part of the error, for example via a rectified reference or gain shaping near t=0. Moderate (inference).

The mean-square reading looks tractable: augment the state with the preview buffer and use a stochastic bounded-real or game argument (inference). That is a reformulation, though, and may already exist, so search first. Step aimed at the original target: for a linear closed loop with x(0)=0, the two gains coincide when w↦z is deterministic. Any gap must therefore come from (A0x+B0u)dW. Test a scalar example for a strict gap.

The full target is a characterization over all monotone structures; likely hard (inference). Use LP duality and exhaustive small cases only to generate or refute conjectures that hold across all structures, for example when maximum contrast is attainable at minimum expansion.

Decidable since 2000. Keep it only if the book specifies a structural criterion; otherwise replace it. If kept, note that K also enters E+BKD1 and C2+D2KC1. State-feedback decoupling has a clean test: im E inside the supremal controlled-invariant subspace in ker C2. Here no supremal invariant subspace is guaranteed (inference). Likely hard (inference).

final_wording: We screened the opening pages [pp. X–Y] of the 2011 information-science volume. Two problems were dropped as already resolved: sorting by transpositions is NP-hard (Bulteau–Fertin–Rusu), and intersection detection for 3D convex polyhedra was settled by Barba–Langerman. Four were excluded as far harder: APN for n≥8, P vs NP, parity games in P, and Tarski's exponential problem. We cannot certify any of the five selected problems as unsolved. 'Open' means only that no resolution was found in the sources searched through 2026-10-14, and all difficulty ratings are inference. (1) Robust SPR synthesis: n≤4 is published, and n=5 and n=6 are publicly claimed in 2026 preprints that we have not independently verified. General n is open in this limited sense and likely hard. (2) P-type ILC with initial errors: the unmodified law cannot keep inputs bounded under repeated initial errors (elementary, not new). Modified P-type laws are open in this limited sense [if the rectification check holds]. (3) Stochastic H∞ preview: the book's norm criterion is non-standard and under-specified. Mean-square results are a reformulation and are only sufficient for the literal criterion with deterministic disturbances. (4) Visual cryptography for general access structures: each instance is a finite LP/ILP, and a general characterization is open in this limited sense. (5) SOF disturbance decoupling: exactly decidable since 2000 (Chen et al.), so open only under a structural reading [state it, or name the replacement]. No original problem has been fully solved. Partial results are listed below with their exact scope.
